messages:
alex_sales: Quick help please — POC customer sending an exported chat blob and were returning 413. They say the file on disk is ~1.2MB but our gateway shows ~2.6MB. Need a repro and short-term unblock.

megan_se: can you paste the curl (sanitized) and say what endpoint/region? Any base64 attachments in the export?

alex_sales: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @chat_export.json
Response: 413, no body. Endpoint is eu-west-1. The export includes inline base64 screenshots and a few HTML snippets. Customer exported from a Windows tool — CRLFs everywhere.

tariq_infra: base64 blobs + CRLF can blow up JSON size. Also double-encoding can happen if client wraps an already-stringified string. Check for extra quoting.

lucy_sre: what upstreams? ALB -> nginx-ingress -> redwood-api. ALB max body is 10MB but nginx vhost had client_max_body_size 1m historically for some demo vhosts. running quick check...

autobot_deploy: sys: nginx-ingress-sales vhost client_max_body_size = 1m; last change 2025-03-02 by ops.

megan_se: two parallel tracks: infra can bump the nginx limit for this route temporarily; engineering can reduce payload size (strip attachments or send references). Also try gzip to avoid transport blowup from escaped unicode.

alex_sales: customer cannot use external S3/storage. They asked if multipart/form-data would be better than raw JSON.

megan_se: multipart can help because you can send attachments as binary parts instead of base64 in JSON. Our API accepts application/json only on /v1/chat right now, though we could accept gzipped JSON. Suggest client-side: 1) remove inline base64 and upload separately to their internal blob store (if they have one), or 2) send a minimal JSON where large blobs are replaced by placeholders and include a short description.

alex_sales: customer says no blob store. Theyre willing to precompute embeddings or a compressed transcript. Any short recipe for summarization?

megan_se: cheap approach: split older messages into ~4k-token chunks, run a concise summarization prompt for each chunk (server-side or client-side), then send only the summaries + last ~3k tokens of raw context. This usually keeps meaning while dropping tokens.

lucy_sre: infra can do a quick change: i'll set client_max_body_size to 8m on the sales vhost and reload the ingress controller. I'll monitor errors for 24h and schedule a revert in 48h if not extended.

autobot_deploy: sys: change applied to nginx-ingress-sales at 11:12 UTC, new client_max_body_size = 8m.

alex_sales: tried re-sending (no base64, replaced with placeholders) and still hit truncation in model output — got 200 but generation cut off mid-sentence.

megan_se: that sounds like model-side truncation (context window). Which model are they pinned to?

alex_sales: pinned to "redwood-open-32k" nominally, but their history after stripping attachments still ~40k tokens.

megan_se: options: 1) recommend long-context model (64k) we host — engineering can estimate cost; 2) implement summarization/retrieval; 3) do a hybrid: recent 4k tokens + top-K retrieval via embeddings.

nina_cs: can we give the customer a quick cost delta for moving from 32k->64k contexts for POC? They asked for ballpark.

megan_se: ballpark: long-context variants are roughly 2x compute per token (depends on attention kernels and batching). If they do infrequent requests, cost might be acceptable for the POC. I'll follow up with a calc given their QPS and avg input+output tokens.

alex_sales: customer wants a temporary engineering workaround so they can demo today without changing model. Any token-aware truncation tricks?

megan_se: implement a token-budgeting function client-side: reserve X tokens for the response (based on expected reply length), then truncate the input from the oldest messages until the token budget fits. Prefer compressing older chat segments via summarization rather than naive truncation. Also remove long quoted HTML and collapse multi-line code blocks to links or short snippets.

lucy_sre: infra note: increasing nginx limit unblocks HTTP, but doesn't affect model context caps. Also watch for slow uploads; large gzipped bodies can still hit proxy timeout if client uses low bandwidth.

alex_sales: customer tried gzip and Transfer-Encoding: chunked — gzip got through and returned 200 but model still trimmed; chunked threw a 411 on their client tool (needs content-length).

megan_se: chunked is unreliable through some corporate proxies. Gzip + token-budgeting + summarization is the fastest path. If they can precompute embeddings we can provide a retrieval snippet recipe.

autobot_deploy: sys: monitoring alert set for sales-vhost body limit anomalies for next 48h.

nina_cs: customer accepts interim plan: (1) client gzip + placeholders for attachments, (2) run client-side summarization for older messages, (3) we keep nginx bump for 48h. They'll follow up about pricing if they want long-context model.

alex_sales: i'll send the checklist and curl examples to their infra team. thanks all. :thumbsup:
